title: Migration Estate Metadata Model
description: Normalized entities discovered from the legacy estate, per master doc §7.1. Discovery Agent (Day 2) emits Table and Pipeline records; Risk Agent (Day 3) emits RiskFinding and updates Table.classification; the deterministic policy engine (Day 3) emits PolicyDecision; Validation Agent (Day 3) emits ValidationResult; Dependency is populated by the Lineage Agent (later day).

classification.description: Discovery emits 'UNCLASSIFIED' by default — PII/sensitivity scoring is the Risk & Compliance Agent's responsibility (master doc §4, §9), not Discovery's.

columns.description: Optional extra detail beyond the §7.1 minimum fields.

is_nullable.description: Whether the source column accepts NULL. Null for adapters that parse static DDL and cannot determine it. Consumed by tools/plan_builder.py to pick a MigrationTarget's null_check_column deterministically instead of hardcoding one — without it there is no non-fabricated way to choose that column for a newly onboarded estate.

upstream_tables.description: Raw table references for the Lineage Agent to resolve into Dependency edges (not itself a Dependency record).

Dependency.description: Populated by the Lineage Agent (later build day); shape fixed now so downstream consumers can be written against it.

PolicyDecision.description: Emitted by tools/policy_engine.py for every agent tool-call evaluation (master doc §5.1, §7.1 'Policy' entity). Deterministic — never produced by an LLM.

RiskFinding.description: Emitted by the Risk & Compliance Agent (master doc §4).

finding_type.description: The five MISSING_IN_ACTUAL..CLASSIFICATION_GAP types are documentation-drift findings (§22.2); SENSITIVITY_SCREEN_DISAGREEMENT is the Gemma-vs-careful-pass disagreement signal (§22.3).

ValidationResult.description: One deterministic reconciliation check (master doc §7.1, §7.3, §11.3). Produced by tools/reconciliation.py — never an LLM judgment call.

MigrationPlan.description: Emitted by the Migration Planner Agent (master doc §4). One per run. Steps are inlined (not $ref'd to a separate MigrationPlanStep definition) so this schema validates standalone, the same way every other definition in this file is extracted and validated in isolation by its owning tool module.

steps.description: Each item: table_id, target_table, execution_order, scheduled (true for the table(s) this run actually migrates; false for catalog tables deferred to a future wave, per §12's 'follow one incident end-to-end' scope discipline), sql_translation_notes.

targets.description: The executable half of the plan (§32's portability model). `steps` describes every catalogued table; `targets` carries the resolved column-level facts the executor, validation, recovery and cutover need — source/target table names, key column, aggregate and null-check columns. Before this existed those facts were module constants in agents/planner/agent.py, agents/orchestrator/orchestrator.py and agents/validation/agent.py, which is what made the estate unswappable. Each item conforms to this file's MigrationTarget definition, deliberately NOT $ref'd: every consumer here extracts one definition node and validates it standalone with no RefResolver (tools/source_catalog.py::_load_schema and its four siblings), so an internal $ref would fail to resolve. tools/plan_builder.py validates each target against MigrationTarget individually — same convention as `steps` being inlined.

plan_hash.description: Binds an approval token to this exact plan (master doc §21.1) — a changed plan invalidates any outstanding approval.

MigrationTarget.description: One table this run actually migrates, fully resolved. Every field is derived deterministically from the discovered catalog (Table.primary_key, Table.columns) plus the Migration Pack's declared type rules — never from a model, per CLAUDE.md's core rule, and never from a hardcoded constant, which is the point of the definition existing.

target_id.description: Stable id within the plan, e.g. 'wwi-sqlserver:Sales.Customers'.

table_id.description: Matches the catalog Table.table_id this target was derived from.

key_column.description: Single-column ordering/identity key from Table.primary_key. A composite primary key yields blocked=true rather than silently taking primary_key[0] — the executor's drop-fraction row ordering and reconciliation's hash check both assume one ordering key, so picking arbitrarily would be quietly wrong.

order_by.description: Deterministic row ordering for extraction; normally equal to key_column.

numeric_column.description: Column for the aggregate-sum reconciliation check, chosen as the first non-key column whose data_type is in the pack's numeric type rules. Null when the table has none.

null_check_column.description: Column for the null-profile check, chosen as the first nullable non-key column (requires Table.columns[].is_nullable). Null when the table has none.

aggregate_check.description: 'not_applicable' when numeric_column is null, i.e. the table has no column eligible for the aggregate-sum check under the pack's numeric type rules. The check is then omitted for this target and the reason recorded — reconciliation.check_aggregate only returns PASS/FAIL, so omitting with a stated reason is the only option that does not fabricate a passing check. The null-profile check's applicability is carried separately by null_check_column being null; the two checks fail independently and must not share one flag.

Incident.description: The 'Incident/remediation' entity from master doc §7.1: signature, root_cause, fix, outcome, reusable_memory. Root-cause narrative may be Gemini-generated (§9's Gemini-eligible column); the fix that is actually applied is always a deterministic, pre-cataloged action, never a model's own proposal executed unchecked.

signature.description: Stable defect fingerprint, e.g. 'row_loss:Sales.Customers' — the key a future run's memory lookup would match on.

root_cause_generated_by.description: 'recalled_memory' means tools/memory_bank.py had a prior confirmed fact for this signature — cited as evidence, but deterministic re-validation still runs before the run is accepted (§21.2 proof 3).

AgentCard.description: A versioned Agent Registry entry (master doc §20.1). Stored at agent_registry/{agent_id}/versions/{version}. The orchestrator's only route to an actor is querying capabilities against APPROVED cards (§20.4) — it never names an agent in code.

capabilities.description: URNs, e.g. 'discovery.catalog.estate'. discover() matches these against a query capability, including a 'prefix.*' wildcard form.

handler.description: dotted 'module.path:function_name' the orchestrator dynamically imports and calls — the mechanism that makes capability resolution real instead of a display list (§20's own framing: 'a registry demonstrates cataloging when the orchestrator cannot function without it').

permissions.description: Mirrors policies/agent_permissions.yaml's shape for this agent — the registry card is generated from that file today (single source of truth); a future day cuts tools/policy_engine.py over to reading this field directly, per §20.4.

MemoryFact.description: A cross-run remediation fact (master doc §5.3, §21.1). Stored globally at memory_bank/{signature} — NOT under a run, per §21.1's session-vs-memory rule: 'Memory is cross-run and holds only durable operational facts.' Recall never bypasses deterministic re-validation (§21.2 proof 3).

MigrationPack.description: Day 10 Phase 3 (master doc §32's portability model). A versioned bundle pairing one estate.yaml source with the classification rules, dialect-translation notes, and default run mode specific to that source family — formalizes what used to be implicit, source-specific assumptions scattered across agent modules. Not itself persisted to Firestore; loaded from packs/{pack_id}/pack.yaml by agents/discovery/run_assessment.py and (for execution-mode packs) agents/orchestrator/orchestrator.py.

estate_file.description: Path to the estate.yaml this pack's source_id is declared in.

source_id.description: Which source in estate_file this pack targets.

classification_rules.description: Path to a data-classification rules file, e.g. policies/data_classification.yaml.

type_rules.description: Source-family data-type behavior, previously the _SCALAR_SAFE_TYPES / _STRINGIFY_VIA_METHOD_TYPES / _STILL_EXCLUDED_TYPES module constants in tools/migration_executor.py. The rules belong to the pack because they are dialect knowledge; the function that applies them stays on the adapter because the mechanism (SQL Server's .ToString()) is dialect-specific too.

numeric.description: Data types eligible to be a MigrationTarget.numeric_column for the aggregate reconciliation check.

scheduled_tables.description: Tables this pack explicitly schedules for execution, with their resolved columns. An explicit entry always wins over catalog-derived inference — this is what lets the committed WWI pack reproduce the previous SCHEDULED_* constants byte-for-byte, making their removal provably behavior-preserving. Omit entirely for a newly onboarded estate and every field is derived from the discovered catalog instead.

target_dataset.description: Overrides BQ_DATASET for this pack; null falls back to the environment default.

ConnectionProfile.description: How to reach one source, by REFERENCE ONLY. This definition deliberately declares no field that could hold a credential value, and additionalProperties is false so one cannot be added by accident — tests/test_contracts.py asserts this directly. The onboarding wizard collects references; tools/secrets.py resolves them at connection time; nothing here is ever persisted to Firestore, returned by the API, or written to a log.

host_env.description: Name of an environment variable holding the host.

password_secret_ref.description: Secret Manager reference, e.g. 'sqlserver-wwi-password' or a full 'projects/{p}/secrets/{n}/versions/latest' path. Never the secret itself.

password_env.description: Name of an environment variable to fall back to when password_secret_ref cannot be resolved (the documented local-dev path). A NAME, never a value.

EstateSource.description: One source system within an Estate. `adapter` names a type registered in tools/adapters/__init__.py's ADAPTER_TYPES; `config` is passed straight through as constructor kwargs, which is why its shape is adapter-defined rather than fixed here.

source_id.description: Unique within the estate. Also the prefix of every table_id this source produces ('{source_id}.{database}.{schema}.{table}') and the Wave Manager concurrency key.

connection_profile.description: Conforms to this file's ConnectionProfile definition (not $ref'd — see MigrationPlan.targets for why). Null for static-file sources with no live connection.

pack_id.description: Default Migration Pack for this source.

Estate.description: A customer's legacy data estate — the unit of onboarding, isolation and authorization (§32.2). Stored at estates/{estate_id} in Firestore, importable from and exportable to estate.yaml so config-as-code and the in-app onboarding wizard describe the same thing. Multi-estate support is what turns this project from one migration into a migration control plane: run documents, Wave Manager concurrency state, connection health and role grants are all scoped by estate_id.

estate_id.description: Stable, unique. Used as the Firestore document id and as the scope key on runs, wave state, connection health and role claims.

status.description: Deletion is soft: an estate referenced by non-terminal runs is DISABLED, never removed, so run history stays interpretable.

sources.description: Each item conforms to this file's EstateSource definition (not $ref'd — see MigrationPlan.targets).

dataset_env.description: Environment variable naming the dataset; falls back to BQ_DATASET.

origin.description: Which authoring path created this document. import_from_yaml refuses to overwrite an estate whose origin is 'wizard' unless forced — that refusal is what lets committed config-as-code and in-app authoring coexist without one silently overwriting the other.
